summary: Redwood AE+SE ran an evaluation and quality-monitoring walkthrough for Brightleaf Finance. Focus was on prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B comparisons, and Console/API workflows. Brightleaf is interested in runbook for spotting regressions after model rollouts and automating alerts tied to prompt sets. Security questions around VPC, KMS, and audit logs were raised; Redwood to share SOC2 and trial org. Next step: 1-week eval comparing Redwood-hosted inference vs OpenAI across 5 prompt sets.
topics: Security: SOC2, VPC, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-21 15:30 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Anita Khanna (Brightleaf - Head of ML), Jared Lee (Brightleaf - Platform Eng), Priya Nair (Brightleaf - Security)

Summary: quick eval/quality monitoring product walkthrough focusing on how Redwood handles prompt sets, regression detection, and A/B comparisons across model variants.

[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Samira, i'll kick us off, diego will do the deep dive into the console and the eval flows. Anita, appreciate you and team carving out time.
[00:18] Anita (Brightleaf): thanks Samira — excited to see the monitoring piece, we've had some real regressions after model upgrades and it's been painful to detect.
[00:28] Diego (Redwood SE): cool, quick agenda: show prompt set management, how to run A/B comparisons, configure regression alerts, and demo the API + console for running evals and surfaced metrics. We'll also cover security briefly.
[00:40] Jared (Brightleaf): sounds good. our constraints: low latency for customer-facing chat (~200ms p50), data residency in us-east, SOC2 compliance, and we want deterministic rollbacks if a rollout causes regression.
[00:55] Samira: great context — those map nicely to the canaries and alerting we show. one note: for the evals we suggest 5-10 representative prompt sets per tokengroup, and Redwood can do an A/B run against a baseline model.

[01:15] Diego: jumping into the console — apologies for small text, let me share screen. First screen is the Eval dashboard: you can create a prompt set by importing CSVs or using our prompt builder. each prompt has metadata tags — intent, expected answer, tolerance (numeric or top-k), and ground truth.
[01:38] Anita: how do you handle paraphrases? our QA often has multiple acceptable answers.
[01:45] Diego: good question — we support fuzzy matching configs: token overlap, normalized edit distance, and custom matchers (regex or small eval scripts). you can also attach multiple ground truths per prompt.
[02:01] Priya (Security): on the data side, anything we upload for prompt sets — is it stored encrypted, and can we keep it in our VPC or on-prem?
[02:12] Samira: yes, for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and on-prem options; for hosted we encrypt at rest and in transit, and we can provide a VPC peering or PrivateLink setup for network controls. we'll share the SOC2 and network diagram after the call.

[02:35] Diego: back to the console: once you have a prompt set you can run an evaluation job. you choose a baseline model (eg: gpt-3x or redwood-omega) and a candidate variant. You can run N-shot or zero-shot. The job produces metrics: exact match, f1, BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, response latency distribution, and a per-prompt score + metadata.
[03:05] Jared: do you capture token-level costs too? we need to understand unit economics for each variant.
[03:12] Diego: yep — cost per call is surfaced; we also show per-token breakdown and a cost delta for the A/B run. that's in the Optimize tab where batching/quantization suggestions live.

[03:35] Anita: show us regression alerts — how would we get notified if a rollout causes a drop in NPS or accuracy?
[03:45] Diego: two layers: first, the dashboard computes delta metrics between baseline and candidate and flags regressions based on thresholds you set, for example drop in f1 > 3% or increase in avg latency > 50ms. second, you can configure alerting channels — slack, pagerduty, webhook. alerts include sample failing prompts and diff traces so engineers can triage.
[04:10] Samira: we also let you tie alerts to rollout policies so an automatic rollback can be triggered if a critical metric breaches.

[04:25] Anita: how noisy are the alerts? previous tools gave too many false positives.
[04:30] Diego: fair — we have configurable sensitivity and group-level thresholds (group by intent, user cohort, or prompt tag). there's also a weekly regression digest vs immediate critical alerts; you can tune for recall vs precision.

[04:58] [screen: A/B comparison view]
[05:02] Diego: here's an A/B run sample we did — baseline is openai-beta, candidate is redwood-optimized-quant. per-prompt table shows baseline score, candidate score, delta, and flags. clicking a row opens the full trace, including token-level timings (note: token timings can be approximate due to ASR in some earlier captures, so small mismatches may appear).

[05:35] Jared: can we export the failing set to our JIRA or ticketing system?
[05:40] Diego: yes, export to CSV or push to webhook that creates tickets — we have a JIRA integration template as well.

[05:55] Anita: on tooling — does Redwood let us define success metrics per prompt set? e.g., for intent routing we only care about intent accuracy, not exact match.
[06:05] Diego: absolutely — you can define per-prompt scoring functions and rollup metrics per set. the UI shows rollup and per-intent performance so you can spot regressions confined to a specific use case.

[06:28] Samira: i'll interject with an example: a merchant support flow where high-confidence answers must be above 90% exact match — Redwood can enforce that as a gating SLA for deployment.

[06:40] Priya: security question — audit logs: how granular are they? we need per-request logs with redaction options for PII.
[06:50] Diego: logs include request/response metadata, timestamps, model variant, and evaluation outcome. we support redaction policies and can store logs in your S3 bucket or forward them to your SIEM. for Private you can keep logs behind your VPC.

[07:12] Anita: what about continuous monitoring? do we run periodic evals automatically after a model auto-update?
[07:20] Diego: yes, you can schedule periodic runs (daily/weekly) and attach rollout hooks so any model promoted to production triggers a smoke eval on chosen prompt sets. if threshold breaches, we send alerts and can auto-revert based on policy.

[07:38] Samira: let's demo an actual regression we seeded. diego, could you run the job?
[07:42] Diego: running now — job queued, running across 200 prompts (~3k tokens total). Estimated finish in about 90 seconds.
[08:10] [job completes]
[08:12] Diego: results: candidate dropped f1 by 4.2% overall and flagged 27 prompts as regression. here's a diff view: for prompt id 214, baseline answer includes account balance remediation steps, candidate omitted the remediation. we'll open that trace.
[08:34] Anita: that's the exact kind of miss we've seen in production. can you show the sample traces with the API call?
[08:40] Diego: sure — here's the trace: request payload, prompt context, model response tokens. note that in our logs some proper nouns are sometimes mis-transcribed (example: 'KV cache' became 'K V cash' in an older transcript) — that's a transcription quirk, but the actual token traces are raw so you can inspect.

[09:05] Jared: for the A/B comparison, how do you control for non-determinism between runs? we want apples-to-apples.
[09:13] Diego: we seed RNG and run same prompt batch simultaneously across variants where possible, and we run multiple iterations to estimate variance. the dashboard shows confidence intervals and p-values for metric deltas.

[09:30] Priya: who has access to eval data in Redwood? RBAC model?
[09:36] Samira: RBAC is standard: org-level admins, project-level editors, read-only viewers. you can restrict who can see PII or raw traces. SSO via SAML/OIDC and SCIM provisioning available for enterprise.

[09:55] Anita: what's the onboarding for the eval flow? do we need to instrument anything in prod?
[10:01] Diego: minimal instrumentation. you can upload historical logs or export a sample of realtime requests through an integration to seed prompt sets. then run the eval jobs and iterate. For automated continuous monitoring we recommend sending a subset of prod traffic to our canary endpoint or running evals against snapshots.

[10:25] Samira: quick pause — any blockers from your side on scope or timeline?
[10:31] Anita: timeline: we'd like a 1-week pilot in the next two weeks; stakeholders include platform and security. main blocker is getting SOC2 and network compliance ok.

[10:44] Diego: that's doable; we'll provision trial org and seed it with a few example prompt sets. we'll also include an A/B job template that compares Redwood-hosted vs OpenAI for your prompts.

[11:00] [switching to Optimize tab]
[11:05] Diego: Optimize shows cost/latency tradeoffs: here we ran the same eval across quantized variants and show expected cost savings and estimated latency improvements. you can click suggestions to apply quantization profiles in Dedicated or Private stacks.

[11:25] Jared: curious about accuracy hit with quantization — do you surface expected regressions?
[11:32] Diego: yes — Optimize recommends profiles and shows historical evals where that profile was applied and the observed delta; you can preview potential regression risk before applying.

[11:50] Anita: for the A/B results, can we get a per-cohort breakdown? e.g., EU vs US customers, or high-value users?
[12:00] Diego: yes — cohorting is supported via prompt tags or request metadata. you can slice by region, user_tier, intent, and more.

[12:18] Samira: quick note on cost: Samira: Redwood provides a usage report and suggestions for batching and prefix caching to reduce token counts for predictable flows.

[12:35] Priya: encryption keys — does the hosted product support CMEK?
[12:41] Diego: hosted supports customer-managed keys for some tiers; Private supports full CMEK and HSM integrations. we'll include specifics in the security pack.

[12:58] Anita: any limitations on size or types of prompt sets? we have some long context prompts (~8k tokens).
[13:07] Diego: you can register long contexts; the runtime supports long-seq optimizations. for very large contexts we recommend chunking and using our embeddings/reranker pattern to reduce eval noise.

[13:30] [brief cross-talk]
[13:45] Samira: ok let's talk outcome measures for the pilot: Anita, what are your success criteria?
[13:53] Anita: 1) Redwood detects regressions automatically with less than 10% false positives, 2) A/B report gives clear cost/perf tradeoffs so we can pick a model variant with equal or better accuracy and cost delta < 10%, 3) security signoff (SOC2 + VPC).

[14:15] Diego: noted — we'll design the pilot to include threshold tuning and an initial triage run to calibrate sensitivity.

[14:25] Jared: about data residency — is there any routing we need to set up for eu customers?
[14:31] Samira: for EU we can pin inference to EU region or provide Private deployment in your region. we'll inline network requirements in the follow-up.

[14:45] Priya: just to confirm: what logs will we receive for audit? full request/response, or masked versions?
[14:52] Diego: configurable: you can choose raw, masked, or redacted; we support automated redaction rules for PII patterns.

[15:05] Anita: anything else in the console we should know?
[15:08] Diego: there are regressions timelines, root-cause suggestions that try to cluster failing prompts by intent or beam, and a sampling tool to replay failing prompts against other model variants.

[15:25] Samira: quick product note: Redwood's canary rollouts can be tied directly to Eval results—so a canary that shows a regression can be automatically rolled back.

[15:40] Anita: costs — can you remind us how pricing works for eval jobs? is it counted as inference?
[15:48] Samira: eval jobs count as inference usage and we bill per token and compute time; for pilots we can provide a usage credit. we'll include pricing in the follow-up.

[16:00] Jared: what's the support SLA during pilot?
[16:05] Samira: Standard pilot support includes SE oncall during business hours, and we can offer a brief 2-week elevated support window if needed.

[16:20] Priya: one last security ask — we need to run a pen test on the integration. is that allowed?
[16:27] Samira: yes, we allow coordinate pen tests on Private deployments; for hosted we can coordinate with our security team and sign a pen test scope. We'll include contact info in the security pack.

[16:45] Diego: wrapping up — demo recap: prompt set management, per-prompt scoring, A/B comparisons, regression alerts with sample traces, Optimize cost/latency tradeoffs, RBAC and security options.

[17:00] Anita: this was helpful, thanks. we'll aim to kick off pilot week of 2025-07-28.

[17:08] Samira: perfect. i'll send the security docs and set up the trial org. diego will seed the prompt sets and the A/B job template.

[17:20] Samira: any final Qs?
[17:22] Priya: none from security.
[17:24] Jared: none.
[17:25] Anita: no, thanks everyone.

[17:30] End recording.
